# CSF shared vocabulary

Source: [architecture.csf](architecture.csf). This dictionary defines the names used in generated diagrams.
It describes a documentation model; it does not verify controller execution or deployed behavior.
Each term has the stable anchor `#term-<identifier>`; linked documents point to it.

| Identifier | Name | Definition | Kind | Home |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="term-observe"></a>`observe` | Observe | Read the available measurements, logs and outputs from an execution. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-retrieve"></a>`retrieve` | Retrieve | Find relevant saved sources, earlier results and relationships. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-choose"></a>`choose` | Choose | Select a proposed action or candidate controller from the allowed choices. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-check"></a>`check` | Check | Apply the configured contract, bounds and admission rules before execution. Passing these checks does not establish physical safety. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-execute"></a>`execute` | Execute | Run an admitted action in its configured environment. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-evaluate"></a>`evaluate` | Evaluate | Compare the result with criteria chosen independently of the candidate being evaluated. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-save_evidence"></a>`save_evidence` | Save evidence | Keep the candidate, observed result and source references so the result can be inspected and reused. This was previously called retain; it does not mean retrain. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-ouroboros"></a>`ouroboros` | Ouroboros | Use evaluated results to propose the next version of an agent's instructions or an allowed workflow. RRSI is its method. Every accepted change is an operator-approved pull request; the grader and held-out evaluations stay outside what it may change. In source it is the mining loop, candace/services/ouroboros: a service mounted into the harness host app that runs every accepted miner over the harness corpus the moment a log changes, pre-checks every mining ticket's proposal at no model cost, launches one fixer per ticket through the harness under a daily budget, runs the merge train and measures the struggle rate and its compounding rate; its ledger is the csf\_ouroboros tables in csfpg and its four cron triggers run on the host's cron service. Fixers launch unattended only when sandboxed launch is available; until then the host turns them on by an explicit flag. | component | planned 355 |
| <a id="term-miner"></a>`miner` | Miner | An accepted extractor and Datalog rule under candace/services/ouroboros/miners: one directory holding extract.ml, rules.dl, labeled fixtures and the backtest its acceptance test regenerates. A miner reads one corpus item (a harness event log, a ticket, a pull request or a file at a revision) into typed facts and derives verdict rows, each carried with its proof. The loop runs every built miner's executable at the knee its own backtest fits and records the findings in the ledger. |  |  |
| <a id="term-precheck"></a>`precheck` | Pre-check | The free check the loop makes before it pays a model for a mining ticket: the ticket's latest proposal must label at least one instance that exists in the corpus and is of a kind the proposed miner's extractor reads (a run directory, an existing issue or pull request other than the ticket itself, or a commit). A proposal that names none is queued for the labeler with the verdict needs\_labels; one that does gets the verdict launch. The csf ouroboros precheck verb runs it by hand. |  |  |
| <a id="term-fixer"></a>`fixer` | Fixer | One harness session the loop launches for one mining ticket whose proposal passed the pre-check: a typed recipe on the fixer model (Haiku), run with the session gates on in a worktree of its own, briefed to finish the ticket's miner and open a draft pull request. The ledger records each fixer's cost, tokens, seconds and outcome; the loop launches at most one per ticket, within the harness's admission and the daily budget, and closes a fixer once its one turn is done. |  |  |
| <a id="term-merge_train"></a>`merge_train` | Merge train | The loop's trigger that runs the merge path (tools/merge-pr.sh) over every ready, non-language pull request, oldest first, once per head: a refused head is commented on with the refusal and retried only after its author pushes a new one. It honors NO-SELF-MERGE: the merger is never an author session, and a pull request whose commits carry the merger's own identity is refused without running the path. |  |  |
| <a id="term-slice_dispatcher"></a>`slice_dispatcher` | Slice dispatcher | The pass that runs the slice graph with no orchestrator: candace/services/dispatch's dispatcher, a cron trigger every minute and again after every merge the merge train makes. Each pass marks merged every slice whose recorded pull request has merged, measures three limits from data and records each with its derivation — the harness's launch check (cores minus the one-minute load, and the disk floor), the mining loop's daily budget, and the provider's rate-limit headroom from the latest rate\_limit\_event in the session logs — and launches the ready frontier (every depends\_on slice merged, no contender running, not held) in critical-path then urgency order, up to the minimum of the three. Pause and resume stop and restart every launch; hold and release keep one slice back; each control is recorded with its reason in csfpg and survives a restart. AddSlice, the controls and the snapshot are typed operations served over MCP and HTTP; csf slice is their client, and every pass writes the snapshot to dispatch.json in the state directory. |  |  |
| <a id="term-struggle_rate"></a>`struggle_rate` | Struggle rate | Harness-fixable struggle episodes per 1,000 agent tool calls per calendar day, with its 95% Garwood Poisson interval, as candace-server #330 measures it. The loop's deterministic reading of a harness event log keeps three of rrsi-mine's nine signals, tool errors, permission denials and exact retries, merged into episodes at the same gap, and counts every episode, since no labeler marks noise here. |  |  |
| <a id="term-compounding_rate"></a>`compounding_rate` | Compounding rate | The weekly growth factor of the struggle rate with its 95% interval: the exponent of a weighted log-linear fit of the weekly rate on the week index over the weeks with at least one struggle and 200 tool calls, exactly #330's trend. It is the loop's objective (#120): the baseline to beat is ×1.156 per week (×1.135 to ×1.177) at 49.9 per 1,000 in the week of 2026-09-28, and exponential improvement is the factor below 1 and staying there. It is recorded as a series and shown on the ops view with its interval and the baseline; it is not estimable under three active weeks, and the same fit per day is the early read until then. |  |  |
| <a id="term-structure_per_intervention"></a>`structure_per_intervention` | Structure per intervention | The loop's internal check (#120): merged enforced structure gained on main per week (session gates, accepted miners and ontology terms, counted from git at the week's end; recorded intents live in csfpg and are not counted yet) over the operator interventions of that week. Until the AFFECT miner labels corrections, the operator-authored messages into sessions stand in for interventions, so the series is marked proxy. The slope of log(y) on the week is the compounding exponent, with its interval; it is not estimable under three weeks. |  |  |
| <a id="term-generic_gate"></a>`generic_gate` | Generic gate | A miner, and every finding it derives, whose rule holds for any harness user: a draft pull request opened late, a sleep loop, a self-matching pgrep. The scope is decided when the miner is accepted and carried on every finding as SCOPE\_GENERIC. A generic finding from an opted-in tenant's sessions may enter the shared miner set once it passes the operator-identifier gate and carries no transcript text, facts and spans only with its instances re-keyed; the tenant record and its opt-in field, default off, are planned. |  |  |
| <a id="term-tenant_gate"></a>`tenant_gate` | Tenant gate | A miner, and every finding it derives, that encodes one operator's intents, rulings or vocabulary, carried on every finding as SCOPE\_TENANT. A tenant finding never leaves the tenant. |  |  |
| <a id="term-mutation_score"></a>`mutation_score` | Mutation score | How well a miner's test tells the miner from its mutants: each mutant is one change to the miner's rules or labels (a body atom dropped, a comparison swapped, the knee written as a score, an atom negated, a rule dropped, two verdict heads exchanged, a label flipped, the split moved); the miner's own checks run on each, a mutant they fail is killed and one they pass has survived; the score is killed over killed plus survived. A mutant the rules check refuses, or one that derives the same verdicts as the original under every knee candidate, is excluded with its reason. The gate holds every miner at or above the floor the template miner measured, rejects a miner whose test lets a surviving mutant change a labeled instance's verdict, and prints the survivor. The ops view shows each miner's score as a series read from the state directory's mutation.jsonl. In source: services/ouroboros/contract/mutate.ml. |  |  |
| <a id="term-labeler"></a>`labeler` | Ouroboros labeler | The service candace/services/ouroboros/labeler: for a mining ticket that names no real instance, it finds candidate spans in the corpus the ticket's miner would read (harness event logs through the file capability; issues, pull requests and commits through the process capability), asks a local model behind the brain contract to label each batch with a verbatim quote, and keeps a positive only when it reproduces: through the ticket's miner when one exists, otherwise by its quote being on the line it names. Every label is a typed ProposedLabel of the ouroboros contract and the run's measurements a LabelerRun, which the ops view's panel shows. It shares the GPU: it yields while another container created with the GPU runs, and each request's keep-alive is derived from the measured gap between batches. The harness binary's label verb composes it. |  |  |
| <a id="term-failure_code"></a>`failure_code` | Failure code | A named, recurring way the agent system fails, declared in this file as a failure\_code with its fault edge, its fault side, the MAST mode it refines and, once one exists, the miner whose rule detects it; the generator projects every code to candace/services/ouroboros/codes. MAST's 14 modes are the seed. A complaint, an operator correction that the operator's own message reads as, is coded by the local model behind the brain contract, and the code is kept only when the model's quote from the complaint is in it verbatim. Complaints no code fits are the residual: the model proposes a code for each, proposals with the same name are counted together, and a proposal becomes a code when it is declared here and regenerated, as AdaMAST induces its codes from traces. The harness binary's ouroboros codes verb codes a corpus, counts complaints per code, edge and side, and records each coded complaint; nothing is injected into sessions. |  |  |
| <a id="term-fault_side"></a>`fault_side` | Fault side | Who owns a failure code's repair, from the interaction-centric taxonomy of agent failures: harness, a session gate or a miner; harness\_environment, a migration or an infrastructure slice; environment or provider, capacity rather than a gate; model, the turn executor's model choice. The code's fault edge is the pair of components, two ontology terms, between which the failure starts. |  |  |
| <a id="term-select_controller"></a>`select_controller` | Select a controller between episodes | Compare candidate controllers' evaluated results and keep or reject them between episodes. Planned: the low-level controller is external and ROS-side, so CSF's in-Go bounded CPU search was removed with its controller interpreter. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-retrain"></a>`retrain` | Retrain | Update a model's learned parameters using training data. This is one possible improvement method, not a required step of every iteration. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-human"></a>`human` | Human or agent client | The caller that supplies a task and policy and uses CSF's exposed operations. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-brain"></a>`brain` | Brain | An agent loop over a large model, reached through an inference provider or API. Brains are external to CSF: CSF defines the brain contract and ships a minimal stub. A brain's proposal is not permission to execute it. | component | planned 346 |
| <a id="term-agent"></a>`agent` | Agent | A named worker: versioned instructions plus a live conversation session, holding assignments and receiving messages at a typed agent address. A proposal from an agent is never permission to execute. Registrations are in memory behind relay.IRegistry until the durable registry, claims and checkpoints are stored through csfpg. | component | planned 346 |
| <a id="term-assignment"></a>`assignment` | Assignment | One task given to an agent definition, with its own identifier and ticket reference. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-checkpoint"></a>`checkpoint` | Task checkpoint | A saved typed task record containing its owner, status, next action, evidence and preceding checkpoint identifier, so another agent can resume the work. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-work_continuity"></a>`work_continuity` | Work continuity | The task checkpoint service at candace/services/workcontinuity. It reads, validates and records checkpoints against a caller-supplied issue source: the HTTP source, or the gh CLI run through the process capability it is granted. It owns no background workers or service lifetime; the Workbench calls it within the existing CSF runtime. | component | candace/services/workcontinuity |
| <a id="term-session"></a>`session` | Workbench conversation session | A conversation and its execution records under a stable identifier. CSF stores Workbench sessions; the current Copilot backend still manages its working context, and a Claude Code turn executor still holds its own transcript: that is the gap the turn executor term names, since CSF is to own the session, its record, its context and its tools. This is distinct from a gotth-live UI connection. | component | candace/services/harness |
| <a id="term-session_suspend"></a>`session_suspend` | Session suspend | The session hypervisor's suspend and resume of a virtual session: suspend ends the session's turn executor process while the session stays open on its recorded real session, and resume opens the executor again on that conversation for the next message, the way a restarted harness resumes a run. Today the agent harness is the hypervisor and suspends a session once it has sat between turns past the idle bound with no turn in flight, nothing queued and no live child in the executor's process group; a session whose executor the process table does not show is kept. The first turn after a resume carries the time to its first token and how long the session was suspended on its receipt, and the session reports suspended while it is. The bound is derived, never set by hand: the knee of the measured gaps between turns in the state directory's run records, reported with its quantile beside every use, with the prompt cache lifetime standing in until two gaps exist. The resident memory of the harness and its executors, the open sessions, the executors alive, the resumes and the time to first token after a resume are one series the harness samples into the state directory's resident.jsonl and the ops view shows. In source: OpenSession.Suspend and Resume in services/harness/session, and services/harness/idle.go and resident.go. |  |  |
| <a id="term-ui_session"></a>`ui_session` | Live UI session | One accepted gotth-live WebSocket connection and the server-side state maintained for that connection. Each connection initializes its own widget state values; a reconnect creates a new session. Separate values can still refer to shared mutable objects. This is not a stored agent conversation or a memory-isolation boundary. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-context"></a>`context` | Context | The information supplied to a model for a particular decision. CSF-owned snapshots and compression remain planned. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-contracts"></a>`contracts` | Shared typed contracts | Protobuf messages, Liquid Proto predicates and OpenAPI operations that define data shapes and allowed calls. Their generators produce bindings and transport code. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-application"></a>`application` | Application | Reserved for a runnable composition whose execution owns a process and runtime. A widget, service, page or web layer mounted inside that process is not another application. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-runtime"></a>`runtime` | Runtime | The execution environment of one application process. It owns the root lifetime and starts and stops the services mounted into it, giving each a scope. Services mount into it; mounting a service adds no runtime. Deployment rule: one runtime per machine; scale by adding machines. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-host_runtime"></a>`host_runtime` | Host runtime | The runtime in source: candace/runtime.HostRuntime, one per process. The binary's main function builds it, grants capabilities to the services it constructs, mounts them and owns the root lifetime. Services start in mount order. By default they stop in the reverse order, each scope canceled and joined in turn; the Concurrent shutdown order instead cancels every scope at once and joins them together. A failing service cancels the runtime with its error as the cause. Readiness is true only between the last start and the first stop. | component | candace/runtime |
| <a id="term-widget"></a>`widget` | Widget | A component of gotth-live that presents typed state and accepts events. Widgets exist within gotth-live; they are not independent components mounted directly into an application. A widget does not own a process or runtime. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-widget_definition"></a>`widget_definition` | Widget definition | One widget as data: a directory widgets/&lt;name&gt;/ holding a dialect document, a binding from one of its streams to the fields of a source the host has, and fixtures. The host checks it (the dialect validates, its refinements hold, an interpreted widget draws all of it, every bound field exists in the source's schema, every fixture renders) and draws it through the dialect interpreter, so it is installed and removed while the host runs and loads no code. A definition that fails a check is refused with every reason and never drawn. |  |  |
| <a id="term-gotth_live"></a>`gotth_live` | gotth-live | The required owner of widgets and their web interaction. It belongs to CSF's web layer and runs within the application's existing process/runtime. | component | candace/pkg/gotth |
| <a id="term-app"></a>`app` | App | A runnable composition of services. Launching an app instance creates an application process; a Go app has its own Go runtime. Mounting another service inside that app does not create another process or runtime. The app owns the root lifetime. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-process"></a>`process` | CSF: one Go application process | One running application with a shared address space. Its host owns listeners, startup, shutdown and any configured worker goroutines. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-service"></a>`service` | Service | The required lifecycle contract for an SDK capability mounted into the caller's process. A service may share its host's lifetime without another scope, goroutine or process, or declare a shorter child lifetime. A service may start goroutines; it owns them and performs its own cleanup: release its resources, stop and join its goroutines, and report failures. Its host triggers shutdown and waits for it; the host does not reimplement the child's cleanup. Whoever composes services owns the lifecycle between them. Borrowed resources keep their declared owner. Common enforcement and migration are pending. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-http_service"></a>`http_service` | HTTP service | In the proposed recursive lifecycle contract, a service that manages an HTTP server and mounted child services. It participates in its parent's startup and shutdown, performs its own server cleanup, and asks its children to perform theirs. The application main function owns the root service's lifetime. Registering routes alone does not implement this contract. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-live_ui_service"></a>`live_ui_service` | gotth-live service | The in-process capability that manages live UI connections and their goroutines for a host app. Its lifetime can span many shorter connections. The current Go type is live.App, a runtime service: each connection's read pump, actor and effects start in a child of its own sessions scope, and its stop sends every connection the going-away close and joins every one of those goroutines with no deadline. It does not require another application process. | component | candace/pkg/gotth |
| <a id="term-database_io"></a>`database_io` | Database I/O capability | Database access granted to a service. The application opens the pool through csfpg (candace/ipc/db/csfpg), the only pool owner; services receive it in their constructors and never close it; the application closes it after the services stop. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-mount"></a>`mount` | Mount | In the proposed ginService.Mount(child) API, attach a child service to the parent's lifecycle: startup, shutdown signaling and waiting for the child to finish its own cleanup. Existing Register(router) only registers HTTP routes and does not supply these guarantees. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-manager"></a>`manager` | Manager | Policy that selects or coordinates services when that decision is dynamic. The name does not create a process or a separate lifetime. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-scope"></a>`scope` | Scope | An explicit lifetime with one owner, cancellation and completion. Cancellation requests shutdown; joining waits until children have exited. In source, candace/runtime.Scope starts goroutines on a service's behalf (Go for a task, GoOwner for a goroutine that must last the scope), nests child scopes, and on join returns every collected error. A goroutine error cancels its scope and is reported to the scope's owner. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-lazy_service"></a>`lazy_service` | Lazy service | An opt-in service lifecycle chosen by the composer: candace/runtime.NewLazyService wraps a service so mounting it starts nothing. The first Use starts it on a child scope and holds a lease for the call. Once no lease is held and the idle timeout has passed, the child scope is canceled and joined, unless the service reports work in hand through IIdleReporter. The next Use starts it again on a new scope. Start errors surface at use time. In architecture declarations, lifecycle lazy is the one case where a call may reach a shorter-lived provider, because the call restarts it. Relay inboxes are the first consumer. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-ownership_transfer"></a>`ownership_transfer` | Ownership transfer | An explicit API agreement that hands responsibility for a specified mutable payload from sender to receiver. After a successful handoff, the sender stops accessing it through retained aliases until ownership is returned. Go channel sends copy values and do not invalidate pointers or deep-copy referenced data. Borrowed dependencies keep their owners; cancellation and submission acknowledgement do not establish completion or return of ownership. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-process_boundary"></a>`process_boundary` | Process boundary | The edge of one process's address space, and the line the tier enum needs between its two same-process tiers (in\_process, kernel\_io) and its two cross-process tiers (host, network). Information that crosses it to another process on the same machine is IPC, the host tier; to another machine, the network tier. A system call that returns to the same process, such as reading a file or the clock, is kernel\_io and crosses no process boundary. Launching a child process goes through proc. The architecture checker checks selected process boundaries in source. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-io"></a>`io` | I/O crossing | Information moving between owners, or state that more than one goroutine can reach and so needs mutual exclusion: both are communication. Data owned by exactly one goroutine, with no lock and no channel, is owned data, not io. The tree that holds io is sorted by tier, one directory per crossing tier: io/inproc (in\_process), io/kernel (kernel\_io), io/ipc (host) and io/net (network), plus io/proto for protocol clients that run over either ipc or net. In-process code never lives under io/ipc or io/net, and an implementation under io/kernel, io/ipc or io/net must reach a real crossing primitive. Planned home candace/io: today the tree is candace/ipc, and slice X2 (#264) moves it once in-flight pull requests drain. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-tier"></a>`tier` | Crossing tier | How far information travels between owners: one ordered enum, narrowest first, in\_process, kernel\_io, host, network. A crossing that touches two tiers reaches the wider one. Agent addresses, the relay's counters, stores and the io directories use this same enum. In source it is candace/ipc.Tier, which names in\_process, host and network today; kernel\_io joins it in slice X2 (#264). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-capability"></a>`capability` | Capability | A value, granted to a service through its constructor, that permits one kind of io crossing; the io directory that holds it names its tier. A service that takes no capability crosses nothing wider than in\_process. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-ipc"></a>`ipc` | IPC | Interprocess communication, in this ontology only: information crossing to another process on the same machine, the host tier. Its home io/ipc holds unix sockets, proc (os/exec) and docker (the Docker Engine socket). Another machine is net, never IPC, and in-process code never lives under io/ipc. The glossary records the broader textbook reading. The directory candace/ipc predates this meaning and still holds every capability until slice X2 (#264) renames it to candace/io and sorts its children by tier. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-in_process"></a>`in_process` | In-process tier | Tier in\_process, the narrowest: anything two goroutines in one process touch, by message passing (a channel, the relay) or by shared memory behind a lock, the shared-memory model of communication. Its io home is io/inproc. The runtime owns this tier: locks and raw sync primitives are permitted only in io/inproc and the runtime. A leaf critical section is in-process io; a lock elsewhere becomes a house-lint finding when slice X2 (#264) lands the gate. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-kernel_io"></a>`kernel_io` | Kernel I/O tier | Tier kernel\_io: a system call whose far side is the kernel, not another process: files and the clock. A file is a kernel store. Its io home is io/kernel (fs and clock). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-inproc"></a>`inproc` | In-process I/O | io/inproc, the home of the in\_process tier: message passing between goroutines (the relay, PipeNetwork); the leaf primitives Cell\[T\] (Load, Store, and Update with a pure func(T) T), Counter, Map\[K,V\] and Snapshot\[T\] (copy-on-write through atomic.Pointer); in-process substitutes for io capabilities and out-of-process stores (pgmem's csfpg.IDB, the model stub, ros's DisconnectedSpine); and the gomock mocks of io interfaces, today in mocks directories beside their packages. Planned: the leaf primitives do not exist yet, and the rest live in their owners' directories until slice X2 (#264). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-kernel"></a>`kernel` | Kernel I/O capabilities | io/kernel, the home of the kernel\_io tier: fs and clock. Today fs is candace/ipc/fs and clock is candace/ipc/clock; slice X2 (#264) creates the directory. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-leaf"></a>`leaf` | Leaf critical section | A lock-guarded section is a leaf only when all three hold. First, while held it acquires no other lock, performs no channel operation and no io, and calls nothing it does not control, so it adds no edge to the lock-order graph. Second, it covers one datum and each operation is a single step, such as a read, a write, an increment or a map get or put, with no invariant spanning two operations. Third, nobody waits on it: no condition variable and no wait for a change. Failing any one makes it a protocol: give the state one owning goroutine and send it messages (house rule CS-5). A leaf is in\_process io and uses the io/inproc leaf primitives (planned, slice X2 #264); raw sync appears only inside io/inproc and the runtime. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-net"></a>`net` | Network capabilities | io/net, the home of the network tier: information crossing to another machine through TCP and UDP dialers and listeners, http and grpc. Today the directory is candace/ipc/net, which grants IListener and IDialer over the host network stack, so a test can replace the kernel with an in-memory pipe; its loopback and unix-socket uses are the host tier. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/net. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-proto"></a>`proto` | Protocol clients | io/proto: clients of a protocol that runs over either ipc or net, such as csfpg, the model providers copilot and claudecode, and ros. A protocol client is granted a dialer and never dials itself; its tier is the tier of the dialer it was granted. Planned: these live under candace/ipc until slice X2 (#264). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-proc"></a>`proc` | Process capability | io/ipc/proc, host tier: the one subprocess gateway and the only importer of os/exec. It owns launch, input and output, cancellation, waiting and cleanup of child processes. Today it is candace/ipc/proc: ILauncher runs or starts a program from an argument vector with an explicit directory, environment and streams, returning a structured result. Each child gets its own process group, or for a terminal its own session; cancellation or Kill ends the whole group or session, and Run and Process.Wait always reap the child. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/ipc/proc. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-docker"></a>`docker` | Container capability | io/ipc/docker, host tier: the Docker Engine reached through its SDK client over the Engine socket on the same machine. Today it is candace/ipc/docker: ContainerHost, whose RunSandboxed runs one container to completion with no network, no capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root and a pids limit, collects bounded output, and removes the container on every path, cancellation included. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/ipc/docker. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-clock"></a>`clock` | Clock capability | candace/ipc/clock, kernel\_io tier: the time source granted to a service as IClock, the current instant and a wait that delivers once a duration has elapsed, so a test can grant a controllable clock. SystemClock is the host's clock; ManualClock moves only when a spec advances it and fires the armed waits in deadline order. The cron service is its first consumer; warden's and the harness's clocks are still service-local. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/kernel/clock. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-http"></a>`http` | HTTP capability | candace/ipc/net/http, network tier: one HTTP server bound to one address and mounted into the host runtime as a service, and the outbound IHTTPClient whose every connection is dialed through a granted socket capability. The listener binds during startup, serves from its scope and drains in-flight requests on shutdown with the shared server shape; the client never reads proxy settings from the environment. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/net/http. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-grpc"></a>`grpc` | gRPC client capability | candace/ipc/net/grpc, network tier: an IClientConnector that opens lazy gRPC client connections dialed through the socket capability. A service calling a remote gRPC API receives a connector and never calls grpc.NewClient itself. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/net/grpc. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-fs"></a>`fs` | File capability | candace/ipc/fs, kernel\_io tier: read-only file access granted as IFiles, the io/fs shape of opening, reading and listing, over one host directory by HostFiles on os.DirFS, and change notification beneath the same directory granted as IWatcher by HostWatcher over the kernel's inotify queue, one bounded subscription per Watch. A service that reads files from the host receives IFiles in its constructor and one that reacts to them changing receives IWatcher too; files compiled into the binary cross no boundary and need no capability, and a test grants an in-memory tree and a gomock watcher whose channel it feeds. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/kernel/fs. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-config"></a>`config` | Config capability | candace/runtime/config: the only reader of the process environment. The binary reads it once and hands values, or the Environment itself, to what it constructs; the binary declares the names as constants and the defaults in the capability call. candace config envcheck compares each Go-built Compose service's environment with the names its binary reads, reporting dead and missing names. Pure value parsing stays in candace/pkg/config. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-pkg"></a>`pkg` | Pure library | candace/pkg: domain-neutral primitives that start no goroutines and cross no boundaries. Code that needs either belongs in runtime or io (candace/ipc until slice X2). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-eventually"></a>`eventually` | Eventually | candace/pkg/eventually: the typed test wait. Await polls a typed value until a predicate accepts it within a named budget and returns that value; Consistently asserts a predicate keeps holding for the budget. Gomega's Eventually is the polling implementation, erased once inside the package. Test-only: it waits in the caller's goroutine and crosses no boundary. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-placement"></a>`placement` | Placement rules | Where a responsibility may live, checked by house lint as advisory locators: every goroutine has an owner responsible for its cleanup, a context-driven exit and a join (CS-15); network listen and dial and gRPC client creation only under ipc, and fork or exec only in ipc/proc, tests included (CS-16, with file placement to follow); PostgreSQL pool and connection creation only under ipc/db/csfpg, blocking, tests included (CS-16-DB); environment reads only in runtime/config or a binary's own config package, tests included (CS-17); and every directory under candace names an ontology term, internal being transparent. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-ratchet"></a>`ratchet` | Ratchet | A comparison that lets a measured count fall but never rise: a change and its base are measured by the same checkers, so only the tree differs, and the change is refused when a count rises. Ratchet mode is the ontology alignment score's (tools/ontology-score.sh --ratchet): a change regresses when the comparable penalty, or any blocking signal (csfc-check, generated-drift, cs-16, unlinked-terms), rises above its base, and the merge path refuses a regressed change before it reaches main. |  |  |
| <a id="term-ontology_alignment"></a>`ontology_alignment` | Ontology alignment | How closely the tree follows the ontology's placement and vocabulary rules, the property the ontology alignment score (tools/ontology-score.sh) measures: a weighted count of findings such as csfc check diagnostics, generated drift, unowned boundary crossings and README terms not linked to their definition, where 0 means every measured signal is clean. The ratchet keeps it from regressing. |  |  |
| <a id="term-deploy"></a>`deploy` | Deploy | The deployment control plane: desired state, placement, operator approval, reconciliation against Warden's fleet view, receipts and its PostgreSQL store. candace/services/deploy is the service, candace/web/deploy its web layer, and candace/app/deploy the application that composes them. It replaces the retired name CandaceOS. | component | candace/services/deploy |
| <a id="term-nodeexec"></a>`nodeexec` | Node executor | The service that applies one approved Compose assignment on one machine under a leader fence. It is the only component given the Docker socket. candace/services/nodeexec is the service and its client, candace/web/nodeexec its HTTP API, and candace/app/nodeexec the thin binary. | component | candace/app/nodeexec |
| <a id="term-harness"></a>`harness` | Agent harness | The service that runs agent sessions: one process per machine runs every session concurrently, each an owner goroutine on a child scope that opens the agent's session for an assignment on a turn\_executor in its own worktree, keeps that executor open across turns, owns the session's record, hooks and event log, and stops at a safepoint when canceled. Its typed operations, generated per api, are SubmitAgentSession, SendAgentSessionMessage, ListAgentSessions, GetAgentSession, CancelAgentSession and StopHarness, plus a live per-session event stream; before a launch it checks a worker cap and a disk floor derived from measured load, free space and run sizes, report-only until sessions have been measured. candace/services/harness is the service (AgentSessionService), candace/services/harness/session prepares and opens one session, candace/services/harness/chat is the Workbench chat over a session, and candace/app/csf/cmd is the one csf application, whose serve verb is the one long-running process and whose other verbs are thin clients of the operations. Deploy's operator turn is one consumer: it runs one conversation backend (Copilot, OpenCode, Ollama or a demo) from a subpackage of candace/services/harness. | component | candace/services/harness |
| <a id="term-infra"></a>`infra` | Infrastructure kit | Deployment material that is not Go: Compose files, installers and shell drivers under candace/infra. It contains no service and starts no CSF runtime of its own. | component | candace/infra |
| <a id="term-deploy_kit"></a>`deploy_kit` | Deployment kit | candace/infra/deploy-kit: the Compose files, installer, fleet driver and deploy-updater scripts that run deploy and nodeexec on machines. Its environment is generated from the Candacefile environment named deploy. | component | candace/infra/deploy-kit |
| <a id="term-httpapi"></a>`httpapi` | HTTP API package | A web-layer package that registers one service's typed HTTP routes on the caller's Gin router. It owns no listener; candace/web/deploy/httpapi and candace/web/nodeexec/httpapi are the deploy and node executor APIs. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-webui"></a>`webui` | Operator web UI | The web-layer package that renders deploy's operator pages and serves their assets: server-rendered HTML with a small browser script. candace/web/deploy/webui is its only instance. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-httpserver"></a>`httpserver` | HTTP engine package | The web-layer package that builds deploy's one configured Gin engine with its middleware. The application binds it to a listener; the package does not open one itself. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-browserroutes"></a>`browserroutes` | Browser route table | The single source of browser-visible paths shared by deploy's operator pages, their script and the HTTP API, so a route is declared once. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-db"></a>`db` | Database backends | ipc/db: one package per database backend CSF reaches, named csf&lt;backend&gt; (csfpg for PostgreSQL; a later backend such as csfduckdb is a sibling with the same shape). Each owns its connections, its schema and migrations, and the queries generated against them; the stores that use them live in services. A backend is a protocol client of an out-of-process store, so slice X2 (#264) moves each to io/proto. | component | candace/ipc/db |
| <a id="term-csfpg"></a>`csfpg` | CSF PostgreSQL backend | candace/ipc/db/csfpg: CSF's PostgreSQL backend: the only pool owner, the schema's generated queries and its migrations; migrations are the only schema source. The binary opens a Pool from Settings it read through its configuration, applies the schema with ApplySchema, and closes the pool after its services stop; a service receives the IDB capability, sqlc's DBTX plus transactions and Ping, in its constructor and queries through New. No Go declares DDL; the tables carry the csf\_ prefix. It is named csfpg, not postgres, so an importer never mistakes it for a driver or another PostgreSQL package. It is the protocol client of an out-of-process store, so its tier is that of the dialer the composer grants: host for a local socket, network for another machine; until slice X2 (#264) it dials through pgx itself. pgmem's in-memory IDB is its in\_process substitute. Slice X2 moves it to io/proto/csfpg. | component | candace/ipc/db/csfpg |
| <a id="term-database"></a>`database` | Own database | candace/services/database: the PostgreSQL container a csf serve host provisions and owns when it is given no -database-config, so CSF's state lives with CSF and never in another project's database. Ensure creates it once through the container capability (a pinned image digest, a named volume, a loopback port probed once and kept, a generated password), records it in &lt;state&gt;/database.json with mode 0600 and returns once its health check passes; later starts reuse it, csf stop leaves it running, and csf db status&#124;start&#124;stop manage it. The housekeeping trigger database\_backup dumps it hourly with pg\_dump into &lt;state&gt;/backups and keeps as many dumps as fit in a quarter of the space above the disk floor, recording that derivation. |  |  |
| <a id="term-schema"></a>`schema` | Schema | A component's SQL migrations, applied in name order by candace/pkg/sqlmigrate and recorded in the component's own version table. CSF's is ipc/db/csfpg/schema: one file, 001\_init.sql, edited in place and assuming a clean database, recorded in csf\_schema\_version. An application that embeds CSF applies its own migrations afterwards, with any tool and its own version table. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-snapshot"></a>`snapshot` | MVCC snapshot | The committed state a transaction reads: PostgreSQL's multiversion concurrency control gives every transaction its own consistent view, unchanged by writers that commit after it began. Planned: today the harness's state is files in its state directory and Go structures in memory (#620). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-serializable_transaction"></a>`serializable_transaction` | Serializable transaction | The only way state changes once all of it lives in PostgreSQL (#620): read a snapshot, write rows, commit. At the serializable isolation level PostgreSQL commits only results equal to some one-at-a-time order. When two transactions would together break a rule each alone keeps (write skew: each sees 15 children and adds one), one is aborted with SQLSTATE 40001 and rerun on a new snapshot. Snapshot isolation, and read committed, PostgreSQL's default, both let write skew commit. A rerun repeats the transaction's body, so nothing with an outside effect, a model call included, runs inside one. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-schema_constraint"></a>`schema_constraint` | Schema constraint | A rule compiled into the schema so no commit can leave a state that breaks it: a CHECK, a foreign key, a unique constraint, or a constraint trigger compiled from a Datalog rule. If every transaction keeps every constraint and the schedule is serializable, every committed state keeps them all. A rule PostgreSQL cannot decide, such as a Lean proof or a build, is checked outside and recorded as a row the constraint requires. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-row_trigger"></a>`row_trigger` | Row trigger | SQL a table runs inside the writing transaction when one of its rows changes: it answers a typed question the rules already decide, refuses an answer only the operator may give, and rings the commit bell. It never calls a model: per row it batches nothing, a model outage would roll back every write that asks, and a serializable rerun would call it again. Distinct from a cron trigger. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-commit_bell"></a>`commit_bell` | Commit bell | PostgreSQL's NOTIFY, sent by a row trigger and delivered only if its transaction commits, so no listener wakes for state that was rolled back. It carries a row's key, never its content; csf wait listens on it and River workers wake on it. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-river_worker"></a>`river_worker` | River worker | A Go worker of River, the PostgreSQL job queue built on pgx (riverqueue/river): it claims a queued job and does the one thing with an outside effect, a JEV batch, an agent turn, a build, a GitHub call or a git push, outside any transaction, then writes the result back in a new one. A job is inserted in the same transaction as the row it acts on. Planned (#620, #622). | concept |  |
| <a id="term-representable_state"></a>`representable_state` | Representable state | A committed state in which every schema constraint holds. The runtime's whole concurrency contract is that state moves only from one representable state to the next, through serializable transactions. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-mock"></a>`mock` | Mock | Generated gomock test doubles of a package's exported interfaces, in a mocks directory beside the package and regenerated by its go:generate mockgen directive. A double replaces a capability in a test; it is not a boundary crossing. A mock of an io interface is an in\_process substitute; slice X2 (#264) moves those to io/inproc. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-agent_address"></a>`agent_address` | Agent address | Where an agent is reached, as a crossing tier: in\_process (the same runtime), host (another process on the same machine) or network (another machine). kernel\_io reaches no agent, so no address carries it. Provider-specific detail is nested inside each. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-model"></a>`model` | Model providers | The ipc subtree ipc/model: the brain contract IBrain and the brain providers behind it, one subpackage per provider, each crossing to its inference provider through a capability its constructor receives. Each real provider is a protocol client: slice X2 (#264) moves copilot and claudecode to io/proto and the stub to io/inproc. | component | candace/ipc/model |
| <a id="term-stub"></a>`stub` | Stub brain | The brain provider ipc/model/stub: canned, deterministic proposals with no model, network or credential, so the harness runs and its specs pass without an inference provider. It is an in\_process substitute; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/inproc. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-copilot"></a>`copilot` | Copilot provider package | The package ipc/model/copilot that implements the brain contract over the Copilot brain provider (vendor): it proposes Copilot agent turns through the existing Copilot adapter's generated Workbench client. A protocol client; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/copilot. | component | candace/ipc/model/copilot |
| <a id="term-host"></a>`host` | Host tier | Tier host: information crossing to another process on the same machine, which is IPC: a unix socket, loopback, a child process through proc or the Docker Engine socket through docker. Its io home is io/ipc. A host agent, such as a Claude Code session, pulls its inbox through the authenticated agent MCP endpoint. Every address type carrying the host tier embeds model.HostTier. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-network"></a>`network` | Network tier | Tier network, the widest: information crossing to another machine; on this fleet, over the tailnet. Its io home is io/net. A network agent pulls its inbox through the authenticated agent MCP endpoint. Every address type carrying the network tier embeds model.NetworkTier. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-claudecode"></a>`claudecode` | Claude Code provider | The ipc/model provider for Claude Code sessions, each an agent loop in its own process on the same machine, addressed at the host tier by session and local socket. ClaudeCodeBrain makes Claude Code a turn executor: each turn is one Claude Code process started through ipc/proc on a session CSF names, with every input and stream-json event forwarded unchanged and logged under the turn trace. A brain opened as a ClaudeCodeSession keeps one process across turns instead: its stream-json input stays open, each Propose writes a turn and reads to its result, an interrupt control request ends a running turn at the executor's next safepoint, and Close ends the input and joins the process. A protocol client; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/claudecode. | component | candace/ipc/model/claudecode |
| <a id="term-ollama"></a>`ollama` | Ollama provider | The ipc/model provider for a local Ollama server, reached over its HTTP API through the http capability its constructor receives, on this host or a neighbour. OllamaBrain proposes one answer per prompt: a system and a user message and, for a typed answer, the JSON schema the server constrains the model to; the answer carries the server's own load, prompt and generation measurements, and every request carries a keep-alive that says how long the model may stay loaded, because sharing the GPU is the caller's decision. It is the provider that costs nothing per token; the ouroboros labeler is its first consumer. A protocol client; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/ollama. |  |  |
| <a id="term-copilotcli"></a>`copilotcli` | Copilot CLI provider | The ipc/model provider for GitHub Copilot CLI sessions, pinned to one Copilot CLI version. CopilotCLIExecutor makes the Copilot CLI a turn executor: each turn is one Copilot process started through ipc/proc on a session CSF names, which Copilot creates on the first turn and resumes on every later one, with the prompt on its standard input. Its assistant messages and turn result are reported in Claude Code's stream-json shape, the result carrying the token and cache usage of Copilot's usage file, so one event log reads the same whichever executor ran. A recipe's Claude Code tool rules are translated to Copilot's tools and permissions, and a rule with no Copilot equivalent refuses the recipe. A protocol client; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/copilotcli. |  |  |
| <a id="term-hfjobs"></a>`hfjobs` | Hugging Face Jobs provider | candace/ipc/hfjobs: the client of the Hugging Face Jobs API, reached over HTTPS through the http capability its constructor receives, for one namespace and one token: run a container on Hugging Face's machines, list, inspect and cancel the namespace's jobs, and read each flavor's per-minute price. It is the provider services/cloud launches burst and probe jobs through; the provider's own timeout is not a stop CSF relies on, since a measured job outlived it (BURST-SESSIONS, #373). A protocol client; slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/hfjobs. |  |  |
| <a id="term-declaration"></a>`declaration` | CSF declaration | The only source a person or agent edits: CSF declarations (terms, kinds, rules, directories, diagrams) and Datalog rules. Everything else in the tree is generated from it or is evidence a run wrote; a change starts here and nowhere else. |  |  |
| <a id="term-generate"></a>`generate` | Generate from declarations | Write every derived file from the declarations: csfc emit, the documentation generator and the decision tree projection. A generated file is never edited by hand; a wrong output is fixed in its declaration and generated again. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-merge_gate"></a>`merge_gate` | Merge gate | The checks a change passes before main: csfc refuses nothing new, regeneration changes nothing, the build and tests pass, and no golden metric falls (seed files, chief violations, derived share). |  |  |
| <a id="term-pull_request"></a>`pull_request` | Pull request | One proposed change on its own branch, opened ready for the merge train once it passes the merge gate locally; never a draft left waiting and never merged by hand. |  |  |
| <a id="term-change_record"></a>`change_record` | Change record | The typed record of one run of the code workflow: the declaration diff, the generated files, each merge gate result, the pull request, the merge commit and the golden metrics before and after. It is how a reused workflow is measured. |  |  |
| <a id="term-jev"></a>`jev` | JEV | A typed judge: one open-weights model (autotrust/JEV-27B-VL on Hugging Face, Qwen3.8-27B with a decision adapter) that answers typed decisions with a calibrated probability for every option, and is the same weights unmodified for free text. One vLLM process serves both, so every decision and every generation shares one cache. |  |  |
| <a id="term-system_one"></a>`system_one` | JEV System 1 | A JEV decision: a kind, a state, a question and its options in (yes or no, one of 2 to 256 options, or a rating 0 to 5), a calibrated probability for every option out, in one forward pass (POST /v1/decide). Decisions from many sessions batch on the same GPUs. |  |  |
| <a id="term-system_two"></a>`system_two` | JEV System 2 | JEV's base weights generating text, optionally reasoning step by step. A turn executor reaches it as its own model provider (Copilot's custom provider), so filling a decision hole needs no outside model and no outside credits. |  |  |
| <a id="term-typed_question"></a>`typed_question` | Typed question | One decision csfc projects from a declaration for JEV System 1: the kind, the state it is asked in, the question and at most 16 options, each option one thing csfc can then write. |  |  |
| <a id="term-decision_hole"></a>`decision_hole` | Decision hole | A typed question no option fits, or one JEV System 1 answered below the measured knee of its calibration: a session fills it on JEV System 2, and what it writes is checked like anything csfc writes. |  |  |
| <a id="term-bootstrap_job"></a>`bootstrap_job` | Bootstrap job | One cloud job (Hugging Face Jobs) that takes a repository archive in and returns an archive whose tree holds every rule: csf mines the repository, csfc asks typed questions, JEV answers, csfc writes, the checks run, and the loop repeats until every rule holds or the job's cap is reached. |  |  |
| <a id="term-turn_executor"></a>`turn_executor` | Turn executor | A turn executor is the external agent loop that carries out one turn: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, whatever the operator picks. It is a decision boundary: which executor runs is the deployer's choice, and CSF is indifferent to it. CSF owns the session, its record, its context and its tools; the executor only executes the turn and reports every event back. Executors are interchangeable behind model.IBrain, as model providers: claudecode is the first and copilotcli the second, a recipe's executor field chooses between them, both run under the same session gates and report into the same event log, and the stub stands in for one in specs. Until CSF stores the session record and owns context and tools, the executor still holds them. | component | planned 346 |
| <a id="term-cost_event"></a>`cost_event` | Cost event | One typed record of one operation in a virtual session's life on real sessions and what it cost: a turn on a warm real session or after the prompt cache expired, a bind, a rebind, a model flip, an idle close, a reopen or a keep-alive, with its tokens by kind (uncached input, cache write, cache read, output), dollars, time to first token and the turn executor memory it released. The session cost model derives them from each run's events.jsonl and names every field it inferred rather than read. In source: CostEvent in proto/candace/harness/v1/costs.proto. |  |  |
| <a id="term-cost_model"></a>`cost_model` | Session cost model | The package candace/services/harness/costs and the harness binary's costs verb. It derives the cost events of every recorded run; measures its inputs (gaps between turns, rebuild cost, the cache lifetime, turn executor memory, price per token kind per model, success per model and task kind), each with its count and 95% interval; and replays each decision over the record with a deterministic simulator: cache keep-alive and idle close as ski rental, a model flip as a metrical task system, placement by shared prefix and by area signature. The chosen parameters, each with its derivation, and the daily series go to costs.json under the state directory, which the Workbench shows. |  |  |
| <a id="term-fleet_hit_ratio"></a>`fleet_hit_ratio` | Fleet hit ratio | h\_fleet: the share of every input token the fleet's turns submitted that the endpoint read from its prompt cache rather than wrote or took uncached. The session cost model reports it per day and under each placement policy. |  |  |
| <a id="term-area_signature"></a>`area_signature` | Area signature | The exact set of repository paths a real session read, edited or searched, and the ontology terms that name a directory on them, taken from its events. A request's area is the paths and terms its prompt names. Area affinity routes a request to the warm real session whose signature covers it best; the session cost model replays that against the router's title overlap and against always opening a new real session, and derives the carried context beyond which a warm session costs more than the exploration it saves. |  |  |
| <a id="term-relay"></a>`relay` | Relay | The agent messaging service: it delivers typed envelopes from one agent address to another agent's in-memory inbox and counts each envelope by the widest tier it crossed. Delivery between goroutine owners is in\_process io: today candace/services/relay, target io/inproc/relay in slice X2 (#264). | component | candace/services/relay |
| <a id="term-intake"></a>`intake` | Event intake | The service candace/services/intake: GitHub activity as the typed candace.intake.v1.Event. Its webhook receiver, mounted in csf serve, verifies each delivery's X-Hub-Signature-256 against github.webhook\_secret, keeps each delivery once by its X-GitHub-Delivery, records every delivery and event on the GitHub event stream (a run directory's events.jsonl that csf events and the mining loop read), queues pull request feedback in the session that owns the branch, marks merges into main on the slice dispatcher, and after an outage asks GitHub to redeliver what it missed; it needs public ingress to the one webhook route. Its poller, the tailnet-side alternative needing none, reads the REST API with conditional requests and delivers through the relay to the agent a static table names. | component | candace/services/intake |
| <a id="term-goroutine"></a>`goroutine` | Goroutine | A Go function executing concurrently inside its application's process. It shares memory with other goroutines; its owner must arrange cancellation and completion. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-thread"></a>`thread` | OS thread | An execution context scheduled by the operating system. Go schedules runnable goroutines onto OS threads; a package name does not assign either one to a CPU core. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-core"></a>`core` | CPU core | A hardware execution resource on which the operating system schedules threads. Placement and latency require observation or explicit configuration. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-bench"></a>`bench` | Workbench | The Copilot-era Workbench: the user entry point for the Copilot adapter's sessions, tools and inspection, with chat, inspection and keyed Kanban widgets. The operator's control plane for harness sessions is the workbench term, which stands beside it; this Kanban is unchanged and stays the Copilot adapter's board. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-ops_view"></a>`ops_view` | Ops view | The page package candace/services/opsview: a gotth-live service whose cards are widget SDK widgets in one keyed collection, each read from a run directory's run record and event log through the file capability and kept current through its watch capability, so a card changes the instant a line lands and nothing polls. Granted the CSF service's operations it is the workbench, which csf serve mounts on its own listeners; without them it is a read-only view. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-host_profile"></a>`host_profile` | Host profile | A typed record the operator edits on the workbench's host panel: a named set of containers to keep running, started when stopped, whether CSF work (the harness's sessions and their build containers, recognized from its run directories) is kept, and whether every other running container stops. Containers the operator protected never stop. Applying one shows its diff, what stops and what starts, before one confirm naming exactly those containers, and records the change set in the state directory's ledger so one tap undoes it. It never removes a container or touches a volume. The host operations in candace/services/opsview apply it, over HTTP and over MCP at csf serve's /mcp. |  |  |
| <a id="term-verified_action"></a>`verified_action` | Verified action | A button whose operation carries its acceptance check: a dry run of the exact operation against the live system and the result it is expected to produce, plus the names a destructive one lists before one confirm. The check runs when the button is installed and again before each render; a button whose check fails is drawn disabled with the reason, so a page never offers a button that might not work. It is the widget SDK's generic primitive in candace/pkg/widget, which every button on the workbench's host panel uses. |  |  |
| <a id="term-workbench"></a>`workbench` | Workbench control plane | The operator's control plane: the gotth-live page csf serve mounts at / on its own listeners, built from the ops view package. Its first screen is phone-first: every harness session as a live card with running ones first, merges and spend today against the mining loop's daily cap, the loop and miner panels, and the dispatch queue. It acts: send a session a message, recorded as the operator's own words; cancel it; mark its pull request ready; merge it through the repository's merge path; and launch a session from a ticket and a recipe template after showing its admission check. Every action is one generated operation of the CSF service, the same one the csf CLI calls over HTTP and an agent calls over MCP at serve's /mcp, so no action exists only in the page, and each is recorded in the session's event log as a typed control action. It succeeds the Copilot-era Workbench Kanban as the operator's entry point without replacing it. |  |  |
| <a id="term-api"></a>`api` | Generated HTTP, CLI and MCP operations | The generated ways to invoke the same CSF operation contracts. Go callers can also compose libraries directly. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-transport_adapter"></a>`transport_adapter` | HTTP/MCP adapter | The CSF Service registers generated HTTP routes with the caller's Gin router and exposes MCP handlers. It owns no listener, process or independent service lifetime. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-mcp"></a>`mcp` | MCP | Model Context Protocol: the tool-discovery and invocation protocol used by agent clients. Registration does not start another service inside an already running CSF host. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-knowledge"></a>`knowledge` | Knowledge and retrieval | Saved documents, source references and explicit relationships exposed through search and graph operations. Coverage depends on what was actually ingested. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-symbolic"></a>`symbolic` | Symbolic relationship | An explicit named connection between identified records, such as a source and an artifact derived from it. It is distinct from similarity in an embedding search. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-compiler"></a>`compiler` | Compiler | The CSF OCaml compilers under csf/compiler: the documentation language, the architecture checker and the API code generator. None compiles a robot controller; the in-Go controller compiler and interpreter were removed because the low-level controller is external and ROS-side. The Lean model in examples/proof covers arithmetic only. | component | candace/csf/compiler |
| <a id="term-github"></a>`github` | GitHub protocol client | The protocol client ipc/github: a library compiled into the binary that uses it, not a service, granted the http capability, so it never dials on its own, starts no goroutine and owns no process. Its client is generated by oapi-codegen from GitHub's own OpenAPI description, pinned by commit and digest and filtered to the operations its allowlist names, one per line; the token comes through the config capability or gh's own hosts file. csf/githubtools registers the same operations as MCP tools on the endpoint csf serve already has, generated from the same filtered description, so a tool and the call behind it cannot drift; the commit gate, work continuity and the csf github verb call the client directly. Slice X2 (#264) moves it to io/proto/github. |  |  |
| <a id="term-ros"></a>`ros` | ROS spine capability | candace/ipc/ros: the ISpine boundary through which CSF submits an Action to the external ROS-side spine and observes it, over the network. Only the stub ships: DisconnectedSpine answers every call with a typed not-connected error, and views render no spine connected instead of failing. Slice X2 (#264) moves the client to io/proto/ros and DisconnectedSpine, an in\_process substitute, to io/inproc. | component | candace/ipc/ros |
| <a id="term-compile"></a>`compile` | Compile | Translate a source representation into another representation while checking its declared rules. Each compiler names its input, output and guarantees; translating documentation does not prove a robot controller. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-workers"></a>`workers` | Configured worker goroutines | Concurrent workers in the shared Go process that call the job ledger's bounded Reconcile pass to submit, inspect and cancel configured jobs. They drive no controller; the spine is reached only through ros. Current durable job dispatch uses PostgreSQL; memory-first dispatch remains planned. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-inspect"></a>`inspect` | Inspection | Operations that expose available usage, duration, job state and saved receipts. Missing data is reported as missing, not measured zero. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-store"></a>`store` | Store | State that more than one owner can reach. A goroutine's own data is owned data, not a store. Every store is io, and its tier is its io tier: an in-process store (io/inproc: Cell, Map, Counter, Snapshot) dies with the process; a kernel store (io/kernel: files) survives a process restart; an out-of-process store, reached through an io/proto client over ipc or net as chosen by the dialer the composer grants (csfpg and PostgreSQL, Redis, artifact storage), survives the process, and the host too when remote. Say out-of-process store, never IPC store. In-process substitutes for out-of-process stores, such as pgmem's csfpg.IDB, live in io/inproc. CSF's configured out-of-process stores are PostgreSQL for records and artifact storage for original bytes; OpenSearch provides searchable document and log views of those sources. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-opensearch"></a>`opensearch` | OpenSearch | The configured search and aggregated-log system. Saved source records can also be used to reconstruct trace observations. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-jobs"></a>`jobs` | Job ledger | candace/services/jobs: the durable record of requests admitted to external executors. The ledger is an out-of-process store: its csf\_jobs tables live in CSF's PostgreSQL schema, reached through the csfpg backend's IDB capability, and pgmem's IDB is its in-process substitute in specs. A job has a kind, an executor, a typed request, a budget reservation, progress in admitted units, a log cursor, cancellation and cleanup evidence, measurements with evidence hashes and trace delivery state. JobLedger\[Spec\] is generic over the request type; executors are capabilities granted through its constructor: AWS Batch as a remote executor submitted at most once, local Docker as a host executor reconciled under an advisory lock. Simulations are one consumer. Real AWS execution still needs configuration and acceptance. | component | candace/services/jobs |
| <a id="term-cron"></a>`cron` | Cron | The cron service, candace/services/cron: the durable in-process scheduler that mounts into the host runtime, fires each declared trigger on its schedule and records every occurrence through csfpg. It is granted its store, its clock and its triggers through options. Start reconciles the declared triggers with the store and starts the scheduling goroutine on the service's scope; every occurrence runs on a goroutine of that scope under a fenced lease; and the scope's join is its cleanup, so shutdown waits for the occurrence in flight and records it canceled. Execution is at least once: an operation uses the occurrence identifier as its idempotency key. The schedule grammar is the pure library candace/pkg/cron. The Workbench's chat schedules are its first consumer; the harness host app mounts it with the housekeeping triggers and the ouroboros loop's four. | component | candace/services/cron |
| <a id="term-trigger"></a>`trigger` | Cron trigger | A named, human-readable schedule with a catch-up policy (none, latest or all) and an overlap policy (skip or allow) that invokes one operation of a mounted service. Its cursor, the next instant it fires at, is a row of csf\_cron\_triggers. A trigger may submit a job; it is not one: jobs is the ledger of requests admitted to external executors. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-occurrence"></a>`occurrence` | Occurrence | One firing of a cron trigger at one scheduled instant, identified by the trigger name and that instant, so the identifier is stable across restarts and retries. It is claimed under a lease the running operation renews, and it ends succeeded, failed or canceled, or is skipped by a catch-up or overlap policy; every state is a row of csf\_cron\_occurrences. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-views"></a>`views` | Prometheus, Grafana and Langfuse | Configured systems for measurements, dashboards and agent traces. CSF owns its Prometheus and Grafana and uses no other project's: csf serve exports every family of services/views's catalog at /metrics and provisions both as containers it owns, with the CSF dashboard as code, where every family has a panel and every panel queries a family. They display available observations; their existence does not imply every operation was traced. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-experiments"></a>`experiments` | Training results and optional MLflow | Saved experiment artifacts and evaluation results, optionally associated with an MLflow run. Autonomous neural training is not demonstrated, and CSF runs no controller search. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-vendor"></a>`vendor` | Copilot brain provider | The existing Copilot model access and file/tool execution loop, reached as one provider of the brain contract. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-web"></a>`web` | Web layer | HTTP routing, typed APIs, browser connections, event delivery, server rendering and browser updates in the shared host. Workbench uses this layer; widget interaction belongs to gotth-live within it. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-widgets"></a>`widgets` | Widget SDK and gotth-live | The SDK defines typed widgets within gotth-live. The Workbench Kanban uses gotth-live-owned card instances in the shared host, and the ops view installs widget definitions live from its checkout's widgets directory. Widgets share host memory, without private heaps or a required goroutine per widget. Shared mutable state needs explicit ownership and synchronization. Every widget effect is joined before its session's teardown runs. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-spine"></a>`spine` | Low-level spine controller | The fast controller that drives hardware. It is external and ROS-side, not part of CSF; CSF reaches it only through the ros capability, whose ROS transport is planned. Until one is granted, CSF reports no spine connected. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-hardware"></a>`hardware` | Consumer sensors and actuators | Physical devices, potentially reached through CAN or other adapters. Simulator success does not establish safe physical operation. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-engine"></a>`engine` | Engine | Not a CSF lifecycle category. Gin Engine and Docker Engine keep their upstream meanings. Curiosity Engine is a tentative product name for the planned improvement loop, not an implemented runtime component. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-source_recipe"></a>`source_recipe` | Agent definition and assignment file | The typed agent.json input, naming the worker, task, ticket, model and repository. Its optional workspace names what the harness needs to run the session itself: the local repository, base and work branch, brief file, allowed tools and pull request title. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-prepare"></a>`prepare` | PrepareAgentAssignment | The generated HTTP/MCP operation and pure Go preparation function that validate a recipe and calculate stable assignment identities without submitting work. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-plan"></a>`plan` | Prepared assignment | An immutable recipe snapshot with content hashes and retry identities. Preparation does not create a session or establish task success. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-requests"></a>`requests` | Generated Workbench requests | Existing generated session and prompt request types populated from the prepared assignment. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-worktree"></a>`worktree` | Session and worktree records | The conversation and isolated repository checkout associated with the submitted assignment: a Workbench worktree, or the git worktree the harness creates at a path derived from the assignment identifier. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-receipt"></a>`receipt` | Assignment receipt | The returned links among agent, ticket, session, turn and worktree, and for a harness run its branch, pull request and trace. A turn identifier acknowledges prompt acceptance; it does not prove completion. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-session_gate"></a>`session_gate` | Session gate | A structural check the harness installs into every session it runs, as a hook the turn executor calls before or after a tool or when it ends a turn: it rejects a forbidden call, such as a shell poll loop, completes a required step, such as opening a draft pull request after the first commit, or refuses a reply, as the reply gate does. Every decision is logged under the session's trace; a rejected call is never executed. | component | candace/services/harness/sessiongate |
| <a id="term-reply_gate"></a>`reply_gate` | Reply gate | The session gate on the turn executor's end-of-turn event. It reads the turn's reply back from the session's event log with the turn's unvetted terms and tool calls, and refuses the reply with a typed reason the turn continues from when a reply to a message with unvetted terms lacks a complete research check per term, when the reply ends on a question the question\_gate refuses, when it reports a number to an operator who asked for a measurement without a measured\_quantity, or when the reply carries a first-person future commitment (I'll, from now on, going forward, until then I will, every time) with no enforcing artifact produced in the same turn: a commit, a gate or hook change, or a ticket item with an owner, or when the reply waits on a background result (waiting on, will follow, once the run finishes) while the turn executor reports no background task running, so no completion can wake the session, or when the turn's operator affect reads high strain and the reply runs past the measured word bound. Its refusals of one turn are bounded, and a reply it cannot read passes and is recorded. candace/services/harness/sessiongate holds it beside the wait, ready and commit gates. |  |  |
| <a id="term-background_result"></a>`background_result` | Background result | The typed record of a turn a background completion started: when a task the turn executor ran in the background ends between turns, the executor starts a turn of its own with no Send, and the harness counts it as the session's next turn and records the task, how it ended, its exit code when the output names one, how long it ran and the bounded tail of its output on the session's event stream. A session whose turn has ended while its executor still runs background tasks is waiting, not stranded: the completion wakes it. |  |  |
| <a id="term-unvetted_term"></a>`unvetted_term` | Unvetted term | A term of an operator-authored message, a chat turn the operator sent or a relayed message marked as the operator's verbatim words, that appears in none of the operator's earlier messages the harness has recorded. A term is a word of the message after code, identifiers, short words and common English are set aside and inflections are folded to one stem; candace/pkg/terms is the extraction, and its parameters were fit on the operator's history with the false-positive rate recorded beside them. The harness computes a message's unvetted terms when the turn is sent, records them as a typed event and puts them into the turn with the research check each requires. |  |  |
| <a id="term-research_check"></a>`research_check` | Research check | The typed record a reply carries for each unvetted term before acting on it: the term, what it is, what it does not do, whether it fits the operator's stated goal (yes, no or partly, with why) and its likely source (agent output, paper, person or unknown). A reply writes it as a fenced block tagged research-check holding one JSON object; the reply gate refuses a reply to unvetted terms that lacks a complete check for each of them. |  |  |
| <a id="term-endpoint_registry"></a>`endpoint_registry` | Endpoint registry | The typed record, in the harness state directory (endpoints/registry.json), of every operator-facing endpoint csf serve has served: the Workbench, the API and MCP, each with its owner, its users and every address it has been served at, and of every address the operator retired, with the address it moved to, the day and the operator's own acknowledgement, which only the operator records, with csf endpoint retire. An address once registered stays registered: csf serve refuses to start, before detaching, without serving every registered address that has no retirement record, either by listening or by a redirect alias it serves itself that sends every request to the same path on its primary port; the session gate on PreToolUse refuses a command that would stop serving one (csf stop without a csf serve in the same command, a kill of the recorded csf serve process, docker stop or rm of an endpoint's container) and names each endpoint with its users; and the Workbench lists the registry. candace/services/harness/endpoint is the library. |  |  |
| <a id="term-operator_affect"></a>`operator_affect` | Operator affect | What an operator-authored message reads as, from a deterministic lexical and structural proxy with no model (candace/pkg/affect): the operator's strain, low or high (shouting, an insult at the agent, or a self-report of strain); the message's kind, a directive, a question or vision; whether it is an operator correction; and whether the operator reports strain in it.
