The harness records it as a typed event on every operator-authored turn, naming the turn whose reply the message answers, so it labels that turn; a high strain puts a notice into the turn and the reply gate bounds the reply's length. Its rules and bounds were fit on the operator's history and backtested against hand labels and self-reports, with the numbers recorded beside them, and a self-report is the ground truth each refit is backtested against. |  |  |
| <a id="term-operator_correction"></a>`operator_correction` | Operator correction | An operator-authored message that flags a mistake the agent made: an insult or a quality verdict, a mining flag, or a reproach or negation opening the message, and never a vision message; the operator affect reads it. The operator correction series pairs corrections per merged slice with merged slices per hour of operator attention, so it cannot be lowered by merging less or by asking the operator more; csf serve exports the corrections the runs record as csf\_operator\_corrections\_total with source affect, beside the hand-labeled window, and the CSF dashboard draws the pair. |  |  |
| <a id="term-question_gate"></a>`question_gate` | Question gate | The session gate on every question an agent puts to the operator: the questions a reply ends on, judged with the reply\_gate at the end of the turn, and the questions of an AskUserQuestion call, judged before the operator sees them. Only meaning, trust boundaries and class membership are the operator's to decide, and such a question names its class; a question in another sub-class (a magnitude, a fact one can look up, a permission the assignment already grants, a house convention) is refused with the resolution the agent owes, such as a derivation plan for a magnitude. A question, or an alternative it offers, that names what a recorded\_ruling excludes is refused as re-litigation. Every question's class and verdict is recorded and counted, and an operator send marked question\_wanted is recorded as an override, the evidence for the gate's false-positive rate. candace/services/harness/sessiongate holds it. |  |  |
| <a id="term-recorded_ruling"></a>`recorded_ruling` | Recorded ruling | An operator ruling recorded through the harness's RecordRuling operation: an identifier, the statement, the alternatives it excludes as phrases, and the ruling it supersedes. The harness keeps them under its state directory and records the ones in force at the start of every turn, so the question\_gate checks the turn's questions and offered alternatives against them; an excluded phrase matches word by word after stemming. |  |  |
| <a id="term-measured_quantity"></a>`measured_quantity` | Measured quantity | The typed record a reply carries when it reports a number to an operator who asked for a measurement: the quantity in the operator's own words, what the reply measured, whether the two are the same and how they differ when not. A reply writes it as a fenced block tagged measurement; the reply\_gate refuses a reported number with no such block, a quantity the operator did not name, a difference left unsaid, or a term introduced for what was measured with no research\_check. |  |  |
| <a id="term-sandbox"></a>`sandbox` | Session sandbox | The per-session confinement the harness applies to every session's turn executor, which otherwise runs as the operator's user. One cgroup v2 leaf per session bounds its cpu, memory and pids and lets cancel kill the whole subtree with one write to cgroup.kill; a Landlock view grants only the session's worktree, run directory and caches; a seccomp denylist refuses ptrace, namespace, mount, bpf and the related syscalls; no\_new\_privs blocks setuid escalation; and the session's Docker access is routed through the docker\_proxy. candace/tools/csf-sandbox is the Rust package that holds the sandbox\_launcher and the docker\_proxy. Landlock does not cover Unix-socket connect, so making the Docker and lxd sockets unreachable is a pending connect wall, a seccomp user-notification filter or a cgroup connect\_unix eBPF program; until it lands the proxy is the routed path, not an enforced boundary. Sandboxed launch is per recipe until the acceptance passes on a host and requires the harness to run in a delegated cgroup. |  |  |
| <a id="term-sandbox_launcher"></a>`sandbox_launcher` | Session sandbox launcher | The single-threaded Rust binary (csf-session-launcher in candace/tools/csf-sandbox) the harness runs as an argv prefix in front of a session's turn executor, started through proc. Given the session's cgroup and policy it joins the cgroup and writes the derived limits, sets no\_new\_privs, applies the Landlock view and the seccomp denylist, then execs the executor, so every process the executor forks is born confined and inside the session's cgroup. |  |  |
| <a id="term-session_container"></a>`session_container` | Session container | The container a harness session runs in by default: one per session, from the session image (bazel/session\_image, the pinned build image plus the executor CLI, gh, jq, Go and csf, its digest pinned in bazel/session\_image.txt), started and removed by the harness through ipc/docker. It runs as 1000:1000 with every capability dropped, no\_new\_privs and no Docker socket, on the default network, under cpu, memory and pids limits derived from measured session peaks; it sees only the session's run directory, the main clone's .git, the shared Bazel disk cache and OCaml toolchain, the worktree's directory of the executor's conversation store, shared with host sessions so either resumes the other's conversation, and the executor's and gh's credentials read-only. A worktree that pins no image runs in the image the last session image build tagged. The executor is attached with docker exec, tools/bazel.sh runs Bazel directly inside it, cancel removes it and every process with it, and its receipt records its cpu and peak memory. Host sessions, which the sandbox\_launcher confines on hosts without Docker, run only by an explicit csf serve flag and are recorded so on their receipt. |  |  |
| <a id="term-docker_proxy"></a>`docker_proxy` | Session Docker proxy | The per-session filtering proxy (csf-docker-proxy in candace/tools/csf-sandbox) the sandbox points a session's DOCKER\_HOST at: one Unix socket that forwards a fixed allow-list of Docker Engine calls to the host socket and refuses anything that would widen the session's authority. It allows ping, version and image inspect; container create only from the pinned image digests, with binds inside the session's own paths and labelled with the session; and start, wait, attach, logs, inspect and remove only on containers carrying that label. It refuses privilege, host namespaces, devices, foreign volumes and any container that is not its own, so tools/bazel.sh builds through it unchanged. |  |  |
| <a id="term-local_job"></a>`local_job` | Simulator container | A configured local CARLA or Isaac container outside the CSF process. Its output bytes stay in the configured artifact volume. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-submit"></a>`submit` | SubmitSimulation | Admit a bounded request and record a simulation job for a configured worker. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-admitted"></a>`admitted` | Recorded simulation job | The persisted identity, requested configuration and current state of an admitted job. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-start_job"></a>`start_job` | Start configured local profile | The worker asks the external container platform to start the selected simulator configuration. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-poll_job"></a>`poll_job` | Read simulator status, progress and logs | The existing worker observes its configured job and records available simulation steps and output references. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-observations"></a>`observations` | Saved simulation observations | Persisted job state, measurements, log records and references to original output artifacts. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-inspect_job"></a>`inspect_job` | InspectSimulation | Read a simulation job's retained state, measurements and artifact references through the generated operation. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-data_structure"></a>`data_structure` | Data structure | A conceptual arrangement of information in a machine or formal language: arrays, trees, graphs, linked lists, hash tables and their abstractions. The physical placement of a data structure in a store is orthogonal to its conceptual shape. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-memory"></a>`memory` | Memory | Physical RAM. The instantaneous contents of an application's address space. Volatile: lost when the process stops or crashes. To be clear about what persists, use store or recall instead of memory, never agent memory or long-term memory. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-recall"></a>`recall` | Recall | Cross-session agent knowledge: retrieved when a new session resumes an agent's work. A capability separate from physical memory and the in-process store, persisted outside the session's address space and specific to one agent identity. | component | planned 365 |
| <a id="term-action"></a>`action` | Action | A discrete behavior or operation a system can perform: moving, computing, retrieving, storing, checking. Distinguished from the mechanism (a hook, a service call, a system call) that carries it out and from the decision (choose) that starts it. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-hook"></a>`hook` | Hook | Advice on an action: code that runs before or after the action, triggered when the action is taken, modifying behavior without changing the action's own definition. The pointcut specifies which actions carry the hook. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-pointcut"></a>`pointcut` | Pointcut | The specification of which actions receive a hook's advice. In an application aspect, a pointcut can name actions at runtime, join points, or patterns like call sites. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-aspect"></a>`aspect` | Aspect | A set of related hooks and pointcuts bundled together, so they can be deployed, modified and removed as a unit. An aspect cross-cuts multiple concerns: it reaches actions in different services, packages and layers by their pointcuts. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-weaving"></a>`weaving` | Weaving | Attaching an aspect's hooks to the actions matched by its pointcuts, so the hooks run when those actions are taken. May occur at compile time, load time or runtime depending on the implementation. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-backtest"></a>`backtest` | Backtest | Running a simulation or a strategy using historical data that occurred in the past, as if the simulation or strategy were live during that period. Outcomes can differ from forward-testing due to selection bias, overfitting and multiple testing; a proper walk-forward test addresses this by partitioning time into out-of-sample periods the model never saw. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-protocol"></a>`protocol` | Protocol | A structured conversation or exchange: a sequence of typed messages and responses following a prescribed order. Agents engage through protocols; gates and tool operations have message semantics given by their message kinds. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-message_kind"></a>`message_kind` | Message kind | The semantic category of a message in a protocol: check (a gate's question), predicate (a fact or condition), theorem (a proven consequence), conjecture (an unproven hypothesis), diff (a proposed change), citation (a reference to evidence), or measurement (a value from observation). Different kinds drive different checks at the receiver. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-provenance_class"></a>`provenance_class` | Provenance class | One of three orthogonal sources of data: δ (delta) is user-supplied; σ (sigma) is computed; η (eta) is aggregated from other data. Every data item belongs to one, fixed at creation. | concept |  |
| <a id="term-humans_zone"></a>`humans_zone` | Human zone | The operator interface and decisions, separate from CSF's automated runtime. Terms and operations within the human zone serve the operator's needs, not CSF internals. | component | candace/humans |

## Retired vocabulary

These words are no longer CSF vocabulary. The documentation checker reports them in linked documents.

| Retired word | Use instead |
|---|---|
| CandaceOS | Name each part by its function: deploy (the deployment control plane), nodeexec (the node executor), the agent harness or the deployment kit. |
| Curiosity Engine | Ouroboros, the planned improvement loop. Engine is not a CSF category. |
| CSF engine | Name the service or application by its function. Engine is not a CSF category. |
| Improve | Ouroboros, the loop step that proposes the next version. |
| github.com/candacelabs/csf/csf | The Go module is github.com/candacelabs/csf; name the package directory you import instead of presenting csf/csf as CSF's import path. |
| PostgreSQL capability | csfpg, CSF's PostgreSQL backend at candace/ipc/db/csfpg, into which the package candace/ipc/db/postgres was folded. |
| csfdb | csfpg: the schema, its migrations and generated queries moved into candace/ipc/db/csfpg. |

## Failure codes

Each failure code has the stable anchor `#code-<identifier>`. Its edge names the two components where the failure starts; its side owns the repair.

| Identifier | Name | Edge | Side | MAST mode | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-mast_disobey_task"></a>`mast_disobey_task` | Disobey task specification | [`assignment`](#term-assignment) → [`agent`](#term-agent) | `model` | FM-1.1 | The agent does not do what the assignment specifies, or does it under constraints the assignment ruled out. |
| <a id="code-mast_disobey_role"></a>`mast_disobey_role` | Disobey role specification | [`harness`](#term-harness) → [`agent`](#term-agent) | `model` | FM-1.2 | The agent acts outside the role its recipe gives it, doing another station's work. |
| <a id="code-mast_step_repetition"></a>`mast_step_repetition` | Step repetition | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`harness`](#term-harness) | `model` | FM-1.3 | The agent repeats a step it already completed. |
| <a id="code-mast_history_loss"></a>`mast_history_loss` | Loss of conversation history | [`harness`](#term-harness) → [`context`](#term-context) | `harness` | FM-1.4 | The agent loses earlier context and acts as if it had not been said. |
| <a id="code-mast_termination_unaware"></a>`mast_termination_unaware` | Unaware of termination conditions | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`assignment`](#term-assignment) | `model` | FM-1.5 | The agent does not know when the work is done and keeps going or stops at the wrong point. |
| <a id="code-mast_conversation_reset"></a>`mast_conversation_reset` | Conversation reset | [`session`](#term-session) → [`agent`](#term-agent) | `harness` | FM-2.1 | The conversation restarts and progress made in it is lost. |
| <a id="code-mast_no_clarification"></a>`mast_no_clarification` | Fail to ask for clarification | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`human`](#term-human) | `model` | FM-2.2 | The agent proceeds on an ambiguous instruction instead of asking. |
| <a id="code-mast_task_derailment"></a>`mast_task_derailment` | Task derailment | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`assignment`](#term-assignment) | `model` | FM-2.3 | The agent drifts from the assignment onto other work. |
| <a id="code-mast_information_withholding"></a>`mast_information_withholding` | Information withholding | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`human`](#term-human) | `model` | FM-2.4 | The agent has information the operator or another agent needs and does not share it. |
| <a id="code-mast_ignored_input"></a>`mast_ignored_input` | Ignored other agent's input | [`relay`](#term-relay) → [`agent`](#term-agent) | `model` | FM-2.5 | The agent disregards what another agent or the operator told it. |
| <a id="code-mast_reasoning_action_mismatch"></a>`mast_reasoning_action_mismatch` | Reasoning-action mismatch | [`model`](#term-model) → [`agent`](#term-agent) | `model` | FM-2.6 | What the agent does differs from what its own reasoning said it would do. |
| <a id="code-mast_premature_termination"></a>`mast_premature_termination` | Premature termination | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`assignment`](#term-assignment) | `model` | FM-3.1 | The agent stops before the assignment's outcome is reached. |
| <a id="code-mast_no_verification"></a>`mast_no_verification` | No or incomplete verification | [`agent`](#term-agent) → [`session_gate`](#term-session_gate) | `harness` | FM-3.2 | The work is reported done without checking it, or with checks that miss what matters. |

## Decision policies

Named decision policies with an optional class ordering and typed knees. A knee is a measurement (its numeric string) or `unmeasured` when no sample exists.

| Policy | Class ordering | Knees |
|---|---|---|
| `routing` | preempt direct interrupt queue | kappa_c = `16`; kappa_u = `0.152`; kappa_q = `unmeasured`; kappa_l = `1.0`; kappa_d = `100GB`; kappa_b = `unmeasured` |
